draft.title: Interdependencies between species
card: Predator-prey
one species (the predator) kills and eats another (the prey). Prey numbers affect predator numbers, and the reverse.
Competition
two or more species use the same limited resource, such as food, water or space. Both are usually harmed, as each has less of the resource.
Mutualism
both species benefit from the relationship, such as a bee that feeds on nectar and pollinates the flower.
Parasitism
one species (the parasite) lives on or in a host and gains, while the host is harmed. Commensalism is when one species gains and the other is neither helped nor harmed.
draft.remember: Ask who gains and who loses: both gain, one gains and one loses, or one gains and the other is unaffected.

a.q: A tick feeds on the blood of a kangaroo and the kangaroo becomes weaker. Which relationship is this?
a.why: The tick gains food from a host that it lives on, and the host is harmed. That is parasitism. It is not predator-prey, because the tick does not kill and eat the kangaroo.
a.clue: Does the tick live on its victim, and is the victim harmed?

b.q: Two species of lizard on an island both hunt the same few insects, and both lizards are now less well fed. Which relationship does this describe?
b.why: Both lizards use the same limited resource, the insects, and both are worse off. That is competition. It is not predator-prey, because the lizards do not eat each other, even though each one does eat prey.
b.clue: Do the lizards eat each other, or share one limited resource?

problems.detail: The remember line sorts relationships into three outcomes (both gain, one gains and one loses, one gains and the other is unaffected). It leaves out competition, where the card says both species are usually harmed. It also lumps predator-prey and parasitism together without saying how to tell them apart, so it splits the ideas more neatly than the card does.

'Which relationship does this describe?' is loose. The lizards hunting insects is itself predator-prey, so a student could defend that option. Asking for the relationship 'between the two lizard species' would remove the doubt.

check.summary: The facts and answers are right: (a) is parasitism and (b) is competition. The remember line leaves out competition (both harmed), and question b should say it means the relationship between the two lizard species, because predator-prey with the insects is also present.
